daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The government has stated it respects the Constitutional Court ruling regarding educational requirements for Vice President Gibran, following controversy over whether his qualifications meet constitutional standards. The court's decision has drawn widespread attention, with activists filing complaints against KPU and Bawaslu over the educational requirements for presidential and vice-presidential candidates. The ruling has sparked debate about legitimacy and constitutional compliance in the current administration.

  • PAN has handed President Prabowo authority to choose the vice-presidential candidate for the 2029 presidential election, describing it as "the best choice in the struggle."
  • Syahganda Nainggolan explained his reasons for accepting the Bakom leadership position, stating "I believe Prabowo is right."
  • The Judicial Commission has condemned the action of an activist who threw botok at a judge in Pati court, calling bribery allegations of Rp 1 billion "demeaning."
  • DPR Speaker Puan Maharani congratulated Milton Dick on his election to lead the Inter-Parliamentary Union until 2029, expressing anticipation for his "breakthroughs and innovations."
  • Jakarta Governor Pramono stated that Jakarta will remain majority shareholder when regional state-owned enterprises are listed on the stock exchange.
  • Law Minister Yusril proposed rehabilitating drug offenders on empty islands using crocodile and pig farming as part of the program.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi arrived in Jakarta for talks with President Prabowo, with the visit marked by fighter jet escorts and student greetings. The two leaders are scheduled to hold meetings on Sunday to discuss bilateral cooperation. The state visit reflects deepening ties between Indonesia and Egypt across multiple sectors.

  • The Indonesian Embassy in Riyadh has advised Indonesian citizens to avoid Riyadh airport following Houthi attacks on the facility.
  • Australia and Indonesia have concluded the Wirra Jaya Ausindo joint military exercise, strengthening bilateral defence cooperation.
  • Indonesia proposed establishing an ASEAN forum for journalistic copyright consultation to protect media rights across the region.
  • KP2MI partnered with Bandung city government to expand job opportunities for Indonesian migrant workers in Japan.

Other

Indonesia has recorded 63,789 workers laid off in a significant wave of terminations affecting the labor market. The layoffs represent a major economic challenge for the government as it seeks to maintain employment stability amid ongoing economic pressures. The scale of job losses underscores vulnerabilities in certain industrial sectors.

  • The Deposit Insurance Corporation revealed that 161 banks have been liquidated due to causes ranging from fraud to competitive failure.
  • A presidential regulation on ride-hailing services has opened the possibility of fare increases following the decree's issuance.
  • Bali police have foiled illegal trade of protected mobula ray species in the province.
  • Forest fires have destroyed 300 homes in Jelutung, Bangka Selatan, while 123 hectares burned in Raja Ampat.
  • The government plans to build three egg and meat processing plants to strengthen food supply chains.
